newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa steps back from highs on NY data.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa steps back from highs on NY data.

text.p: Nearby LIFFE cocoa futures stepped back from early run-up to end Monday tightly mixed on lack of follow-through buying, traders said.
Values were helped by trade buying in the morning and some arbitrage buying against New York in the afternoon.
But the buying fizzled out towards the close as the New York market also slipped from its early peaks.
Traders said the lower-than-expected drop in latest New York's September open position was cited as a factor behind the retracement.
The data showed the September open position falling by just 4,303 contracts to 34,302 at the close of business on Thursday.
"We thought the specs might have gone out," said one. Both London and New York futures were hammered by specs long liquidation last week, and the data showed that they still have some selling to do.
LIFFE's September fell one stg at 1,038 stg a tonne after an intraday high of 1,052 stg. It cleared the immediate 1,044 stg but lacked stamina to challenge the next resistance at 1,067.
On the downside, the technical picture could turn negative if September breaks below the key 1,000 stg support.
Earlier, traders said the initial rally this morning was seen a technical correction to the sharp fall seen late last week.
"After the 170 stg sell-off in just over two days , it's not surprising that we rallied a bit," said one.
London regained some composure on Friday after taking a tumble earlier in the week, which saw September falling to a low of 1,000 stg on Thursday from a one-year-high of 1,170 on Tuesday.
It recovered to touch a high of 1,040 on Friday. Thursday's sell-off came on the back of aggressive spec and fund-led long liquidation.
Volume stood 6,169 lots, with interest centred on September, December and March.
On the fundamental front, the second-quarter German cocoa grind fell 3.5 percent to 57,401 tonnes but well above earlier expectation of up to seven percent lower.
There were no real surprises in the UK and Dutch figures released on Friday.
